# Project status

Last updated 2026-10-29. Statuses: `COMPLETE` (exists and verified), `IN PROGRESS`, `BLOCKED` (needs decision, data, permission or resource), `DEFERRED` (postponed by instruction).

## Milestones

| Milestone | Status | Deliverables | Verification evidence | Remaining blockers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Audit and setup | COMPLETE | Separate project directory; `README.md`; this tracker; `config/config.template.json`; `schemas/feature_schema.json`; `schemas/label_schema.json`; `docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md`; `docs/DECISIONS.md` | Files exist; schemas are loaded and enforced by the tests | — |
| B. Model pipeline | COMPLETE (synthetic-verified) | `encoding`, `models`, `calibration`, `schema` (validation, info status), `pipeline.predict`, JSON serialisation with checksum, CLI `predict` | 68/68 tests pass (`docs/test_results.txt`), covering missing features, unknown and unseen categories, malformed records, prohibited inputs, insufficient information, save/reload identity, tamper detection | Feature extractors deliberately not built (needs data and decisions) |
| C. Baselines and evaluation code | COMPLETE for listed items (synthetic-verified); gaps below are IN PROGRESS | Four models; publisher-disjoint split with diagnostics; AUPRC, AUROC, Brier, log loss, calibration slope/intercept, reliability table, NDCG@k, hit@k, within-publisher AUROC with publisher-resampled interval; AUPRC/AUROC by publisher type and action type; paired bootstrap (two-way, claim, publisher); outcome classification; error analysis; shuffled-pairing control; markdown and JSON reports | Smoke run `outputs/synthetic_smoke/` (stamped SYNTHETIC); tests for every metric, split disjointness, family merging, reproducibility, outcome classes | See "Known gaps" |
| D. Methodological decisions | IN PROGRESS | `docs/DECISIONS.md`: six project-owner decisions recorded (O1–O6, mentor approval not recorded), conflicts and file-level implications listed, remaining decisions tabulated by decider and blocking stage | Config deliberately unchanged, so `fha.cli status` still lists 18 blockers | Mentor confirmation of O1–O4; remaining decisions in DECISIONS.md §2 |
| E. Data readiness and training | DEFERRED, then BLOCKED | Data-manifest template; real-mode guards | Real-mode run refuses: unresolved decisions, unapproved rules, missing or unauthorised manifest, synthetic or AI-labelled data (tested) | Dataset construction deferred until holidays; decisions in D |
| F. Final evaluation | BLOCKED | Evaluation code ready; test lock implemented | — | Needs E |
| G. Package | BLOCKED | `fha.cli package` (refuses synthetic or unevaluated runs, tested); draft `docs/MODEL_CARD.md` | — | Needs F |

## Known gaps (not yet implemented)

| Item | Status | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Temporal split | BLOCKED | Implement only if decision `temporal_split_required` is `true` and claim dates are reliable |
| Annotator-derived oracle-feature diagnostic (validation only) | BLOCKED | Decision `annotator_feature_diagnostic_allowed` |
| Hard-negative subset metrics | IN PROGRESS | Needs an agreed definition of "hard negative" (same type or topic, not first-hand) |
| Debiased calibration error, mixed-effects sensitivity model | DEFERRED | Optional in the design |
| Embedding-based near-duplicate grouping | BLOCKED | Would need a model download (not permitted); lexical Jaccard used |
| Validation-stage seen-publisher diagnostic (O6) | BLOCKED | Design to be confirmed (DECISIONS.md §0.1); small code change once agreed |
| `candidate_origin` metadata and per-origin reporting (O5) | BLOCKED | Waits for the candidate-generation protocol |
| Line-ending policy (`.gitattributes`) so schema hashes survive checkout | IN PROGRESS | Proposed in DECISIONS.md §1 item 8; not applied |

## Smoke-test observations (synthetic; mechanics only, not evidence)

- The pipeline runs end to end; all four models are scored on identical pairs; zero publisher/family and claim-group overlap between training and held-out sets.
- **Design finding:** with hold-out fractions of 0.5, pair pruning discarded 965 of 1,679 usable pairs (57%) because candidate publishers recur across claims. Real-data sizing and the hold-out fractions need a decision.
- Calibrators fitted on validation make validation calibration figures in-sample; the report now says so and keeps pre-calibration values.

## Change log

| Date | Change |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-10-29 | Project created; schemas, config, pipeline, baselines, evaluation, CLI, 68 tests, docs. Added per-category metrics and within-publisher interval. Smoke run executed on synthetic fixtures. Verified that no file in the frozen experiment was modified (all its recent modifications predate this work). |
| 2026-10-29 | Git initialised in this directory only; `.gitignore` excludes data, annotations, outputs, models, caches and secrets; baseline commit `0bf11fc`. Project-owner decisions O1–O6 recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` with conflicts, implications and remaining decisions; no config, schema or code changed. |

## Boundaries kept

No dataset search or construction; no annotation; no external API calls; no package installation; no downloads; nothing read from or written to `Source_Aware_Misinformation_Detector`. All synthetic outputs are labelled as such and the real-mode guard refuses synthetic records.

docs/DECISIONS.md.content:
# Decisions

Each methodological decision maps to a key under `decisions` in `config/config.template.json`. A real run refuses to start while any key is `null`. **No configuration value has been changed to reflect the decisions below**; Section 1 lists the changes they would require. Nothing here records mentor approval unless it says so explicitly. The values in `config/synthetic_smoke.json` are placeholders that exist only to exercise code.

Status vocabulary: **OWNER-DECIDED** (specified by the project owner; mentor approval not recorded) · **OWNER-PROPOSED** (owner's intended approach, explicitly provisional) · **UNRESOLVED** (no decision) · **DESIGN-PROPOSED** (proposed in the design documents, not yet confirmed).

## 0. Project-owner decisions (recorded 2026-10-29)

Source: the project owner's message of 2026-10-29. Mentor approval: **not recorded for any item**.

| # | Config key | Decision | Status | Mentor confirmation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| O1 | `positive_bases` | `INSTITUTIONAL_ACT`, `OFFICIAL_RECORD`, `ORIGINAL_RESEARCH`, `DIRECT_OBSERVATION` are the intended positive bases | OWNER-PROPOSED (current proposed definition) | **Required** (owner flagged it) |
| O2 | `record_keeper_rule` | `designated_only`: for a statistic, positive only if the publisher is the designated record-keeper for that statistic, not merely an official body | OWNER-DECIDED | Recommended |
| O3 | `quotation_rule` | `content`: judge authority for the substantive content of a quoted statement, not for the fact that it was said | OWNER-DECIDED | Recommended |
| O4 | `self_report_rule` | `positive_with_interested_flag`: an organisation may be first-hand for information about itself, flagged `INTERESTED_PARTY` | OWNER-DECIDED | Recommended |
| O5 | `candidate_source` | Documented retrieval process **plus** curated additions; exact protocol to be confirmed | OWNER-PROPOSED (provisional) | Required once the protocol is written |
| O6 | (evaluation protocol) | Examine seen-publisher performance as a diagnostic first, then unseen-publisher generalisation. Publisher-disjoint unseen-publisher evaluation remains the **primary** generalisation test. Test results are never used to tune the model or select features | OWNER-DECIDED (principle); diagnostic design UNRESOLVED (see 2) | Recommended |

### 0.1 Conflicts found and proposed corrections

| Conflict | Where | Smallest safe correction (not applied) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The *Technical Design* doc's recommended working definition left `DIRECT_OBSERVATION` **out** of the positive class pending mentor decision; O1 includes it | *First-Hand Authority Model: Technical Design* §4.3 (Claude Docs) | Record here that O1 supersedes the design recommendation **pending mentor confirmation**; leave the design doc unchanged as a historical record |
| `config/synthetic_smoke.json` uses three positive bases (no `DIRECT_OBSERVATION`) | Synthetic placeholder config | None needed: placeholders only, and the synthetic generator never emits `DIRECT_OBSERVATION`. Optionally align for consistency |
| O6 says "seen-publisher first". The current code evaluates only **unseen** pairs at the validation stage, and evaluates seen and unseen **test** pairs together at the single test opening. Read literally, "examine test seen-publisher results first, then decide" would allow test results to influence later choices | `src/fha/pipeline.py` (`run`, `render_markdown`) | Define the seen-publisher diagnostic on **validation** seen-publisher pairs (`val_seen`, already produced by the split) before the test is opened. At the single test opening, report `test_seen` and `test_unseen` together, with no changes between them. Needs a small code change and tests (Section 1, item 7) |
| The real-mode guard treats any non-null config value as resolved; it cannot distinguish "owner-decided" from "mentor-approved" | `pipeline.real_mode_blockers` | Add a `decision_approvals` block (`decided_by`, `approved_by`, `date` per key) and require `approved_by` for label-defining keys (O1–O4). Needs owner agreement before implementing |

## 1. Implications of the owner decisions (files that would need to change)

None of these changes has been made.

| # | Decision | File / setting | Required change | Implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | O1–O4 | `config/config.template.json` | Set `positive_bases` to all four bases; `record_keeper_rule: "designated_only"`; `quotation_rule: "content"`; `self_report_rule: "positive_with_interested_flag"` | Do this only once approval status is settled; entering values removes four real-mode blockers |
| 2 | O1 | Labels and evaluation | `DIRECT_OBSERVATION` positives (e.g. news outlets with reporters on scene) enter the positive class | More news-type positives; publisher-type priors become weaker; annotation needs strict evidence rules for observation. Report results with and without `DIRECT_OBSERVATION` as a sensitivity analysis |
| 3 | O2 | `config/role_rules.draft.json` | Already consistent (`OFFICIAL_STATISTIC → STATISTICS_OFFICE` only) | The rule and the features use **publisher type** as a proxy for "designated record-keeper". Where a ministry or central bank is the designated producer, the proxy is wrong. The annotation manual needs a procedure for verifying designation; a future relation feature (`designated_record_keeper`) would need a documented source (research item) |
| 4 | O3 | Annotation manual; `action_type` extractor spec; `schemas/feature_schema.json` description text | Quoted claims are classified by the action in their **content** (e.g. `OFFICIAL_STATISTIC`); `UTTERANCE` reserved for claims about the act of speaking | No schema-level change; `speaker_relation` is expected to carry little positive weight for quoted statistics |
| 5 | O4 | Annotation manual | State which basis a self-report receives (proposed: `INSTITUTIONAL_ACT` for its own acts and conduct, `OFFICIAL_RECORD` for its own filed records); always add `INTERESTED_PARTY` | No schema change (flag already exists). Error analysis already reports flagged pairs |
| 6 | O5 | Data records; reports | Add a top-level metadata field `candidate_origin` ∈ {`retrieval`, `curated`} (never a model feature); report metrics and positive rates by origin | Curated additions risk making positives easy to find (curators add likely authorities). Selection bias must be measured by comparing origins |
| 7 | O6 | `src/fha/pipeline.py`, tests | Add a validation-stage seen-publisher diagnostic on `val_seen`; order the report seen → unseen; keep the single test opening | Small code change; no change to the primary test |
| 8 | Reproducibility (found during Git setup) | `.gitattributes` (new) | Add `* text=auto eol=lf` for `*.json`, `*.py`, `*.md` | Git's global `core.autocrlf` will check files out with CRLF line endings. `bundle.json` stores the feature schema's SHA-256 and refuses to load if it changes, so a fresh Windows clone could not reload a model trained elsewhere. Fixing the line-ending policy keeps hashes stable |

## 2. Remaining unresolved decisions

"Blocks" means the earliest stage that cannot responsibly start until the item is decided. Verified against `config/config.template.json` (all keys `null` except as noted) and `config/role_rules.draft.json` (status `DRAFT_UNAPPROVED`).

| Item | Why it matters | Decided by | Blocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mentor confirmation of O1 (`positive_bases`) | Defines the target | Mentor | **Data collection** (annotation manual) |
| Mentor confirmation of O2–O4 | Label rules; the guard cannot yet record approval | Mentor (owner has decided) | **Data collection** if the mentor disagrees |
| Designated-record-keeper verification procedure (from O2) | Annotators need a rule for establishing designation | Owner drafts, mentor approves | **Data collection** |
| Exact candidate-generation and curated-addition procedures (O5) | Negatives, selection bias, ranking metrics | Owner drafts, mentor approves | **Data collection** |
| `role_rules.draft.json` approval, version and hash | Baseline 1 must be frozen before labels are seen | Owner + mentor | **Data collection** (before labels exist) |
| `available_features` | Determines what is extracted and from which dated sources | Owner + mentor | **Data collection** |
| `temporal_split_required` | Requires reliable claim dates and dated knowledge-base snapshots to be collected | Mentor | **Data collection** (what metadata to record); temporal split code not implemented |
| `merge_corporate_families` | If true, `publisher_family_id` must be collected | Mentor | **Data collection** (metadata); training (split) |
| `min_annotator_agreement` | Pilot pass/fail rule must exist before the pilot | Mentor | **Data collection** (pilot annotation) |
| `annotator_feature_diagnostic_allowed` | If true, annotators must also record feature values | Mentor | **Data collection** (annotation form); diagnostic not implemented |
| `cannot_judge_policy` | Training target (proposal: `exclude`, with two sensitivity runs) | Mentor | **Training** |
| `hub_max_claim_share` | Composition of held-out publishers | Mentor | **Training** (split) |
| `test_unit_fraction`, `val_unit_fraction` | Pruning cost (57% of pairs discarded in the synthetic run at 0.5); affects how much data must be collected | Owner + mentor | **Data collection** (sizing); training (split) |
| `score_limited_pairs` | Unknown-value bias handling | Mentor | **Training** |
| `per_claim_weighting` | Training objective | Owner (low risk) | **Training** |
| `calibration_acceptable` | Recalibration trigger | Mentor | **Training** |
| Seen-publisher diagnostic design (O6) | Must not let test results influence choices | Owner + mentor | **Final evaluation** (pre-registration) |
| Hard-negative definition and metrics | Robustness metric not yet defined or implemented | Mentor | **Final evaluation** (pre-registration) |
| `delta_min_auprc` and its justification | Without it the outcome is `NOT_CLASSIFIABLE` | Mentor | **Final evaluation** (must be fixed before test labelling) |
| Guard support for recording approvals (Section 0.1) | Distinguishes owner decisions from mentor approval | Owner | Training (real-mode run) |

## 3. Proposed in the design and implemented (DESIGN-PROPOSED; confirm or reject)

| Decision | Where |
| --- | --- |
| L2 logistic regression, lbfgs, no class weights in the main model | `models.LogisticModel`, `config.model.class_weight` |
| One explicit interaction: `action_type × publisher_type`, cells kept only with ≥ `min_count` training pairs | `schemas/feature_schema.json` `derived_interactions`, `encoding.Encoder` |
| Missing values kept as an explicit `UNKNOWN` level; `NOT_COMPUTED` shares that column but is reported at inference | `encoding`, `pipeline.predict` |
| Information status rules (`INELIGIBLE`, `INSUFFICIENT`, `LIMITED`, `SUFFICIENT`) | `schema.info_status` |
| Hyperparameters (C, `min_count`) by log loss on grouped, publisher-disjoint inner folds; ties to simpler | `pipeline.tune_lr` |
| Platt recalibration on validation only, triggered by `calibration_acceptable` | `calibration`, `pipeline.fit_all` |
| Primary metric AUPRC on unseen-publisher test pairs; primary comparison claim-conditioned vs publisher-only | `config.evaluation` (consistent with O6) |
| Two-way bootstrap primary; claim-only and publisher-only also reported | `bootstrap` |
| Outcome classes SUPPORTED / UNSUPPORTED / INCONCLUSIVE / HARMFUL / NOT_CLASSIFIABLE | `bootstrap.classify_outcome` |
| Test opened once (lock file) | `pipeline.run` (consistent with O6) |

## 4. Implementation choices made in code (not in the design; reviewable)

| Choice | Reason | Alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full one-hot (no dropped reference level) | L2 makes coefficients identifiable; simpler contributions | Reference coding |
| Inner CV = repeated grouped publisher-disjoint holdouts, not strict k-fold | Strict k-fold with publisher-disjointness is not generally possible | — |
| Claim groups stratified only by "contains a positive" | Keeps positives in every split | Also stratify by action type or date |
| Near-duplicate grouping = token Jaccard ≥ 0.8 on `claim_text`, plus explicit `claim_group_id` | No embedding model download permitted | Embedding similarity + manual review |
| Ranking ties broken by `pair_id`; number of claims with ties reported | Deterministic | Expected metrics over tie orderings |
| Classification threshold for error analysis = max F1 on validation | Never chosen on test | Fixed threshold |

## 5. Questions to take to the mentor

1. Do you confirm all four positive bases, including direct observation (O1)? Should results also be reported without it?
2. Do you confirm the designated-record-keeper, quotation-content and self-report rules (O2–O4)? How should annotators verify that a body is the *designated* record-keeper?
3. Is excluding `CANNOT_JUDGE` acceptable as the main analysis, with the two sensitivity runs?
4. What exact candidate-generation and curated-addition protocol, and how should selection bias between the two origins be assessed (O5)?
5. Should the seen-publisher diagnostic run on validation seen-publisher pairs before the test is opened (O6)?
6. Corporate families and very common publishers in the hold-out? Which hold-out fractions, given the pruning cost?
7. Is a temporal test required?
8. Which features will genuinely be available, and from which dated sources?
9. Should `LIMITED` pairs be scored? May an annotator-feature diagnostic be run on validation only?
10. How is a "hard negative" defined for the robustness metrics?
11. What minimum meaningful difference, agreement minimum and calibration range, and how are they justified?

docs/REAL_DATA_AND_TRAINING_PLAN_DRAFT.m.content:
# Real-data collection and training plan (DRAFT, NOT APPROVED)

**Written 2026-11-02.** This is a plan only. **No real data has been collected, no labels exist, no model has been trained on real data.** The 68/68 passing tests and the smoke run in `outputs/synthetic_smoke/` show that the *code mechanics* work on synthetic fixtures. They say **nothing** about real-world performance.

Nothing here changes `config/config.template.json`, the schemas, the role rules or the code. Items marked **[DECISION]** must be settled (and, where noted, mentor-approved) and recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` before the stage they block. Items marked **[PROPOSED]** are this plan's suggestions.

This project stays independent of `Source_Aware_Misinformation_Detector` (see §14 for the one future interface).

---

## 1. What the model predicts (from the repository)

For a **claim–publisher pair**, `p_first_hand = P(first-hand authority | claim, publisher, eligible features)`: the probability that this publisher has first-hand standing to establish the claim's **central factual proposition**.

It does **not** predict: whether the claim is true; whether a page is relevant or supportive; whether the publisher is generally reliable; how popular or often-retrieved the publisher is (`README.md`; `schemas/feature_schema.json` `prohibited_keys`).

## 2. What a claim–publisher pair is

One record = one claim (text, date, speaker, location) × one candidate publisher (an organisation, account or person resolved to a stable `publisher_id`, optionally a `publisher_family_id` for corporate groups). Every pair has the ten features in `schemas/feature_schema.json` (or the sentinels `UNKNOWN` / `NOT_COMPUTED`) and, for training, one human label per `schemas/label_schema.json`.

## 3. First-hand authority, operationally

A publisher is **FIRST_HAND_AUTHORITY** for a claim if it holds one of the positive **bases** for the claim's central proposition:

| Basis | Operational test | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `INSTITUTIONAL_ACT` | The publisher performed the act the claim is about (issued the policy, passed the law, made the ruling, took the action) | A ministry for a claim about its own regulation |
| `OFFICIAL_RECORD` | The publisher is the **designated** keeper of the record or statistic (O2: designation, not just "an official body") | The national statistics office for the unemployment rate it compiles |
| `ORIGINAL_RESEARCH` | The publisher produced the study or dataset the claim relies on | The journal or research group for a reported finding |
| `DIRECT_OBSERVATION` | The publisher directly witnessed the event (O1; **mentor confirmation required**) | A news outlet whose reporters were on the scene |

Rules already decided by the owner (mentor approval **not** recorded): O2 designated record-keeper only; O3 for quotations, judge the **content** of the quote, not the act of saying it; O4 an organisation can be first-hand about itself, always flagged `INTERESTED_PARTY`.

**NOT_FIRST_HAND_AUTHORITY** reasons: `REPORTS_OTHERS_ACT`, `EXPERT_COMMENTARY`, `REPUBLISHER_OR_AGGREGATOR`, `UNRELATED`, `OTHER`.
**CANNOT_JUDGE** reasons: `UNKNOWN_ENTITY`, `AMBIGUOUS_PROPOSITION`, `ROLE_CHANGED`, `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`.

---

## 4. Dataset schema

Already defined and enforced by code; summarised here.

| Field | Source | Model input? |
|---|---|---|
| `pair_id`, `claim_id`, `claim_group_id` | construction | No (IDs and grouping) |
| `claim_text`, claim date, speaker, location | claim source | Text is not a model feature in the current LR design; used by extractors |
| `publisher_id`, `publisher_family_id`, `publisher_resolved` | publisher resolution | Grouping / eligibility |
| 10 features: `action_type`, `claim_scope`, `claim_topic`, `publisher_type`, `publisher_jurisdiction_level`, `actor_relation`, `speaker_relation`, `jurisdiction_match`, `remit_match`, `active_at_claim_date` | extractors (§7) | **Yes** |
| `candidate_origin` ∈ {`retrieval`, `curated`} **[PROPOSED, O5; needs a small code change]** | construction | **Never** a feature; used for bias reporting |
| `label`: `final`, `basis`, `not_fha_reason`, `cannot_judge_reason`, `flags`, per-annotator records, `confidence` | human annotation | Target |
| `is_synthetic` | construction | Must be `false` for real runs |

---

## 5. Data sources and collection methodology

### 5.1 Claims **[PROPOSED; DECISION]**

**Recommended primary source: AVeriTeC *train* split (3,068 claims, CC BY-NC 4.0).**
- *Why:* decontextualised real-world claims with speaker, date and country, which match the features this model needs. It is research-licensed, and the research group already knows the data.
- **Exclusion:** all **500 AVeriTeC dev claims** are excluded (not only the reserved 180). The dev split is the source-aware project's development and evaluation material. Keeping it out means this model can later be used as a feature there without leakage (see §14). This extends the manifest's existing `excluded_sources` entry.
- AVeriTeC verdict labels, justifications and QA evidence are **not read** for this project (prohibited keys). Claim text and metadata only.

*Alternatives for the mentor:* ClaimReview-tagged fact-checks (wider topics; licence varies by publisher), or a hand-collected set from official press releases (cleaner, but costly and biased toward official sources).

### 5.2 Candidate publishers (O5: retrieval + curated) **[DECISION: exact protocol]**

Per claim, proposed:
1. **Retrieval origin.** From the claim's AVeriTeC train URL list (`data_store/urls/train_urls.zip`: URLs only, no 62 GB knowledge store needed), take the distinct publisher keys. **Ignore the `type` and `query` columns entirely** (they mark gold documents and gold questions). Sample up to *n_r* keys (proposed 6) with a fixed seed, **blind to order and type**. *Caveat to report:* the URL lists were partly generated from gold-derived queries, so they are enriched with relevant publishers.
2. **Curated origin.** A curator who has **not** seen the retrieval candidates writes down up to 2 publishers they believe could be first-hand (e.g. the agency named in the claim). Recorded as `curated`.
3. **Hard-negative origin [PROPOSED, links to the hard-negative decision]:** up to 1 publisher of the same `publisher_type` as a likely authority but a different jurisdiction or remit (e.g. another country's statistics office). Recorded separately so it can be analysed or dropped.

All origins are labelled by the same blind annotation process. **Positive rates and model metrics are reported by origin** (curated candidates are expected to be easier positives; this is a selection bias that must be measured, not hidden).

### 5.3 Publisher resolution

Map each key to a `publisher_id` (organisation-level), and optionally to a `publisher_family_id` (corporate group; needed if `merge_corporate_families=true`). Use Wikidata QIDs where available (snapshot date recorded); unresolved publishers get `publisher_resolved=false` and are scored `LIMITED`/`INELIGIBLE` per the schema rules.

---

## 6. Inclusion and exclusion criteria **[PROPOSED]**

**Claims: include** if the claim states a checkable factual proposition with an identifiable subject; English text; claim date present.
**Claims: exclude** if in any AVeriTeC dev claim (all 500); pure opinion/prediction with no factual proposition; satire-identification claims where the only question is "is this satire?"; near-duplicates of an already-included claim (grouped, not dropped, if they're kept).

**Pairs: include** each sampled candidate. **Exclude** candidates that are search pages, URL shorteners, archives or file hosts (`web.archive.org`, `bit.ly`, generic CDN domains), since they are not publishers. Social-media *platform* domains are excluded, but **accounts** on them (e.g. `twitter.com/<handle>`) are valid publishers.

---

## 7. Feature availability **[DECISION: `available_features`]**

Features must come from **extractors that never see the label** (and never from the annotators who label, unless as the separate, validation-only annotator-feature diagnostic).

| Feature | Proposed extractor | Dated source to record |
|---|---|---|
| `publisher_type`, `publisher_jurisdiction_level` | Wikidata P31/P17/P131/P1001 → frozen `publisher_type_map`; manual coding of unmapped publishers by a person not labelling FHA | Wikidata snapshot date |
| `action_type`, `claim_scope`, `claim_topic` | Rule/keyword coder or a separate pre-coder; O3 content rule applied to quotes | Coder version |
| `actor_relation`, `speaker_relation` | Entity linking of the claim's actor/speaker vs the publisher's QID (same/parent/subsidiary via P749/P355) | Wikidata snapshot |
| `jurisdiction_match`, `remit_match` | Claim location vs publisher jurisdiction; frozen `topic_remit_map` | Map version |
| `active_at_claim_date` | Wikidata inception/dissolution dates vs claim date | Snapshot |

Whether an LLM may be used as an *extractor* (not as an authority predictor, which is prohibited) is a **[DECISION]**. If allowed, its prompt and version are frozen before labels exist.

---

## 8. Annotation guidelines (outline for the annotation manual) **[PROPOSED]**

Annotators see: the claim text, date, location, speaker, and the publisher's identity (name, website, Wikidata description). **Not shown:** AVeriTeC verdict, justification, gold evidence, candidate origin, any model output, retrieval rank.

Decision procedure per pair:
1. **State the central factual proposition** in one sentence (stored for audit only; prohibited as a feature).
2. **Classify the proposition's action type**, applying O3 (quotes judged by content).
3. **Ask: did this publisher perform the act / keep the designated record / produce the research / directly observe the event, for *this* proposition, in *this* jurisdiction and time?**
   - Yes → `FIRST_HAND_AUTHORITY` + basis (+ `INTERESTED_PARTY` if it is about itself; `PARTIAL_ASPECT` if it covers only part of the proposition).
   - No → `NOT_FIRST_HAND_AUTHORITY` + reason.
   - Can't tell after a bounded check (proposed ≤ 5 minutes, using the publisher's own site and Wikidata) → `CANNOT_JUDGE` + reason.
4. **Designated record-keeper (O2):** accept designation only from a citable source (statute, the statistics office's own release calendar or methodology page, official open-data portal); record the URL. **[DECISION: the mentor approves this procedure]**
5. Flag `CLAIM_FAMILIAR` if the annotator already knows how this claim was fact-checked.
6. Confidence 1–5.

The manual includes 10–15 worked examples using **invented** publishers, covering each basis, each negative reason, quotes, self-reports and role changes.

---

## 9. Annotation quality and inter-annotator agreement

- **Pilot (before the main collection):** ~40 claims (≈ 300 pairs), **two independent annotators**, then adjudication. The pilot is used only to refine the manual and is **not** used for training or test. It is discarded or kept as a separate "pilot" set.
- **Agreement measures:** Cohen's κ on `final` (3-way, and binary FHA vs not-FHA); Krippendorff's α if more than two annotators or missing labels; agreement on `basis` among agreed positives; per-action-type breakdown; confusion between annotators.
- **Pass rule [DECISION: `min_annotator_agreement`]:** must be fixed **before** the pilot. Common conventions treat κ ≥ 0.6 as "substantial" and κ ≥ 0.8 as "almost perfect". This is offered as context, not decided here. If the pilot fails, revise the manual and re-pilot on new claims.
- **Main collection:** double annotation on a random ≥ 20% (proposed), single on the rest; agreement reported on the double-annotated part; disagreements adjudicated; unresolved → `final = null` (never a target).
- **Annotators:** human only; AI-generated labels are invalid under `label_schema.json`. Who the second annotator is (peer, mentor, paid) is a resource **[DECISION]**.

---

## 10. Sampling strategy and sizing **[PROPOSED; sizing DECISION]**

- **Claims:** stratified random sample from eligible train claims, stratified by AVeriTeC `claim_types` and by country (US vs non-US) for coverage. Used for sampling only, never as features. Fixed seed.
- **Size:** provisional target **300–400 claims × ~7–9 candidates ≈ 2,000–3,500 pairs**, to be confirmed after the pilot gives (a) the positive rate and (b) the pair-pruning loss of the publisher-disjoint split. The synthetic run lost **57% of pairs at hold-out fractions of 0.5**, so either collect more or lower `test_unit_fraction`/`val_unit_fraction` **[DECISION]**.
- **Effort (rough):** ~1–2 min per pair → ~50–100 h for one annotator on 3,000 pairs, plus ~20% for double annotation and adjudication.

## 11. Train / validation / test split and leakage prevention

Already implemented in `src/fha/split.py`; the plan adopts it:
- **Publisher-disjoint** (and family-disjoint if merging is chosen): test publishers never appear in training. This is the primary generalisation test (O6).
- **Claim-group-disjoint:** a claim and its near-duplicates (token Jaccard ≥ 0.8 + explicit `claim_group_id`) sit in one split only.
- Proportions 60/20/20 (config), with `val_seen`/`test_seen` and `val_unseen`/`test_unseen` subsets.
- **Hub publishers** (appear with many claims) are capped by `hub_max_claim_share` **[DECISION]**.
- **Temporal split:** only if `temporal_split_required=true` **[DECISION]**; code not implemented.
- **Test is opened once** (lock file). **Seen-publisher diagnostic on validation** before the test opens (O6 correction in DECISIONS.md §0.1; small code change pending).
- **Other leakage blocks:** prohibited keys rejected at load; features from extractors frozen before labelling; role rules frozen and hashed **before any label is seen**; `candidate_origin` never a feature.

## 12. Models

**Baselines (already implemented, synthetic-verified):**
1. `role_rules`: hand-written tiers (**must be approved and frozen before labels exist**).
2. `type_prior`: smoothed P(FHA | publisher_type).
3. `publisher_only_lr`: L2 logistic regression on publisher features.

**Proposed final model:** 4. `claim_conditioned_lr`: the same learner plus claim and claim×publisher features (one interaction `action_type × publisher_type`).

**Why logistic regression is the right final model here:** a few thousand pairs, ten categorical features and a research question about *which relations matter*. LR is well-calibrated, interpretable (coefficients map onto the authority definition) and hard to overfit. A transformer cross-encoder over (claim text, publisher description) is a possible **exploratory** follow-up, but only after the primary analysis and only on the same splits.

## 13. Training procedure, evaluation, error analysis

- **Training:** grouped, publisher-disjoint inner CV over `C ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10}`, `min_count ∈ {1, 3, 5}` by log loss; ties go to the simpler model; Platt recalibration on validation only if outside `calibration_acceptable` **[DECISION]**; `CANNOT_JUDGE` handled per `cannot_judge_policy` (proposed: exclude, with the two sensitivity runs) **[DECISION]**.
- **Primary metric:** AUPRC on **unseen-publisher** test pairs. **Primary comparison:** `claim_conditioned_lr` − `publisher_only_lr`, two-way (claim × publisher) bootstrap interval; outcome class needs `delta_min_auprc` fixed in advance **[DECISION]**.
- **Secondary:** AUROC, Brier, log loss, calibration slope/intercept, reliability table, NDCG@k and hit@k per claim, within-publisher AUROC, metrics by publisher type and action type, seen vs unseen, by `candidate_origin`, with/without `DIRECT_OBSERVATION` positives (O1 sensitivity).
- **Controls:** shuffled-pairing control (already implemented): a model that does not beat it is not using the claim.
- **Error analysis:** false positives by publisher type (e.g. news outlets wrongly rated first-hand), false negatives by basis, `INTERESTED_PARTY` pairs, `LIMITED`-information pairs, hard negatives.

## 14. Interface with the source-aware project (future, optional)

The first-hand authority model could later provide an authority feature to the source-aware verdict classifier (`Source_Aware_Misinformation_Detector/docs/proposals/verdict_classifier_training_proposal_DRAFT.md`). That is only safe if:
- no AVeriTeC dev claim (500) is in this project's data (§5.1);
- scores for any claim this project *trained* on are produced out-of-fold (cross-fitting) before they are used as features elsewhere;
- this project never reads source-aware frozen artifacts, reserved claims, gold labels, probes or scoring materials (already in the manifest's `excluded_sources`).

## 15. Compute

All modelling is CPU-only scikit-learn/numpy and runs in minutes on the current laptop. The real costs are **human annotation time** and **Wikidata extraction** (network, cached, snapshot-dated). Disk need is small (< 1 GB), but C: currently has ~2.1 GB free.

## 16. Reproducibility and documentation

Frozen before labelling and recorded in `docs/DATA_MANIFEST.json`: feature schema, label schema, `publisher_type_map`, `topic_taxonomy`, `topic_remit_map`, `role_rules` (hashes); KB snapshot dates; guideline version; annotator IDs (pseudonymous); agreement statistics; usage rights. Apply the `.gitattributes` LF policy (DECISIONS.md §1 item 8) **before** any hash is recorded. The model bundle stores its schema hash and refuses to load on mismatch (already implemented).
